known_facts_book1: A prominent cotton manufacturer, owner of three mills, officer of the Légion d'honneur and member of the Conseil général.
Spent the whole Empire as the head of a 'benevolent opposition', purely to sell his eventual support to the regime at a higher price, by his own account.
Sent six hundred thousand francs to England for safekeeping, as insurance against the war.
Is one of the two men, along with the count, who go to speak to the Prussian officer on the travelers' behalf and are refused.
Reflects, listening to Mme Follenvie's plain complaints about the war, that the manpower wasted on soldiering could enrich a country if put to industrial use instead.
Weeps with laughter, along with the count, when Loiseau reveals what he saw and heard at the inn corridor keyhole.
Discusses stocks and business terms with the count in the coach once they finally leave Tôtes.

known_relations_book1.Mme Carré-Lamadon: His wife, much younger than him.
known_relations_book1.le comte de Bréville: Fellow notable among the travelers; goes with him to petition the Prussian officer.

known_facts_book1: Much younger than her husband; described as the 'consolation' of well-bred officers garrisoned at Rouen, implying an eye for handsome soldiers.
Faints from hunger in the coach before Boule de Suif's food is shared, and is revived with a few drops of wine given by the older nun.
Privately thinks she would refuse the Prussian officer even less readily than Boule de Suif does, when the travelers joke about it.
Goes pale and shivers, as if imagining herself taken by force, when Mme Loiseau argues the officer could simply have taken any of the married women instead.
Remarks that the Prussian officer is rather good-looking and regrets he is not French, once they see him in the street.
Laughs a little too easily the night Boule de Suif gives in, which her own husband's rival Mme Loiseau notes with suspicion.

known_relations_book1.la comtesse de Bréville: Fellow traveler; the two women chat about mutual society friends, including Mme d'Étrelles, once the coach leaves Tôtes.

not_in_this_book: Mme Carré-Lamadon defends Boule de Suif
Mme Carré-Lamadon is the officer's mistress
